shots.full: Same café as the first reference image, the same painting on the same wall. Close shot from across his table: Barry sits chest-up at the red formica table, both hands already wrapped round one chipped mug of tea held just above the table. His phone lies face down on the table beside his plate, untouched. He looks up past the camera, fed up, mouth slightly open mid-word. Over his shoulder, soft, the lower half of the gilt-framed painting and the mint-green tiles under it. A red plastic sauce bottle out of focus in the near foreground, a half-eaten fried breakfast in front of him. Camera at table height. Light: cold blue daylight from the steamed window on his left, a warm yellow strip light above. Barry is dressed exactly as in his portrait reference. Unretouched 35mm film still, rich saturated colour, fine grain, uneven real skin. 16:9. Thanks.

Close among a crowd behind a steel barrier at dusk, rain falling. At the front a woman in her thirties in a wet black raincoat, dark curly hair stuck to her forehead, screams across the gap, mouth wide open, one fist up. Beside her, each one a different person: a tall Black man in his twenties in a grey hoodie under a denim jacket, short beard, shouting; a grey-haired woman in her sixties in a purple anorak and round glasses, pointing; a stocky South Asian man in his forties in a navy work fleece, thick moustache, both hands on the barrier; a skinny teenage girl in a yellow cagoule with a red fringe, clapping; a heavy man in his fifties with a ginger beard and a tweed flat cap. Everyone further back is hooded, under umbrellas or turned away, faces lost in rain and shadow. Camera low on the other side of the barrier, the out-of-focus yellow shoulder of a police jacket in the lower left foreground. Behind them, the columned front of an old bank. Light: one orange sodium street lamp above and behind them, the white glare of a police floodlight from the right on their faces. Rain in the light. No flags, no coloured smoke, no readable text. Unretouched 35mm film still, rich saturated colour, fine grain, uneven real skin. 16:9. Thanks.

Barry stands at the front of a crowd behind a steel barrier at dusk, holding up a cardboard sign that reads WE CAN'T AFFORD TO LIVE HERE in thick black marker, shouting back across the gap. Around him, each one a different person: a wiry man in his thirties in a black tracksuit and a baseball cap, jabbing a finger across the gap; a big Black woman in her fifties in a pink fleece, braids tied up, shouting; a young lad in a paint-spattered white overall, shaved head and freckles; a short white-haired woman in a green quilted coat, thin-lipped, gripping her handbag strap; a broad East Asian man in his forties in a navy security guard's jacket, arms folded on the barrier. Everyone further back is hooded or under umbrellas, faces lost in rain and shadow. Camera high and close above the barrier, looking down at their upturned shouting faces, rain falling through the light. Light: an orange sodium lamp behind the camera, the white glare of a police floodlight raking from the left. No flags, no coloured smoke. Barry is dressed exactly as in his portrait reference. Unretouched 35mm film still, rich saturated colour, fine grain, uneven real skin. 16:9. Thanks.

Same café as the reference image. Close on the gilt-framed oil painting of the soldier on the wall above the mint-green tiles, seen at an angle from below, a curl of steam from a tea urn drifting soft across the lower edge. No people. Light: a warm yellow strip light above, cold blue daylight from the steamed window. Unretouched 35mm film still, rich saturated colour, fine grain. 16:9. Thanks.

Same café as the reference image. The dented chrome tea urn on the worn counter with steam curling from its spout, a row of odd chipped mugs and a stack of saucers beside it, the steamed window soft behind. Camera low at counter height. No people. Light: a warm yellow strip light above, cold blue daylight from the steamed window. Unretouched 35mm film still, rich saturated colour, fine grain. 16:9. Thanks.

Same café as the reference image. The steamed-up café window with rain running down the glass, a red plastic sauce bottle and a salt cellar on the sill in front, the columned front of a grand old bank blurred across the road outside. No people. Light: cold grey-blue daylight through the glass, the warm yellow strip light reflected in it. Unretouched 35mm film still, rich saturated colour, fine grain. 16:9. Thanks.

Same café as the reference image. An empty red formica table: a half-drunk mug of tea, a crumpled paper napkin, a sauce bottle and a salt cellar, the chairs pushed in, the mint-green tiles soft behind. Camera at table height. No people. Light: a warm yellow strip light above, cold blue daylight from the steamed window. Unretouched 35mm film still, rich saturated colour, fine grain. 16:9. Thanks.

From high up between the stone columns of a grand old bank at dusk, looking down at the street in front of it. Two crowds of ordinary people press against two lines of steel barriers, facing each other across an empty strip of wet tarmac where a thin line of police in yellow jackets stands with their backs to the bank. Both crowds are mixed: Black, South Asian, East Asian and white people, men and women, teenagers to pensioners, hoods, flat caps, headscarves and umbrellas. Every face is turned to the other crowd; nobody looks up at the bank. Foreground: the edge of a stone column, out of focus. Light: orange sodium street lamps and the white glare of a police floodlight from the left. No flags, no coloured smoke, only a few handwritten cardboard signs too small to read. Unretouched 35mm film still, rich saturated colour, fine grain. 16:9. Thanks.

Same vault as the reference image. Low on the concrete floor inside the vault: a steel trolley stacked with shrink-wrapped bricks of purple twenty-pound notes is already halfway through the open round steel vault door; of the man pushing it only black suit trousers and polished shoes show. No faces. Light: one caged amber work lamp, deep bottle-green painted steel and brass catching it, the purple of the notes rich in the light. Unretouched 35mm film still, rich saturated colour, fine grain. 16:9. Thanks.

Same vault as the reference image. Close on a steel shelf packed with banded bricks of purple twenty-pound notes: two hands in black leather gloves already pressing one more brick into the last gap, the cuffs of a dark suit at the edge of frame. No faces. Light: one caged amber work lamp, deep bottle-green painted steel and brass catching it, the purple of the notes rich in the light. Unretouched 35mm film still, rich saturated colour, fine grain. 16:9. Thanks.

From directly above: a steel trolley piled high with banded bricks of purple twenty-pound notes and red fifty-pound notes on a concrete floor with a yellow painted line; one black-gloved hand is already lifting the top brick. No faces. Light: one caged amber work lamp, deep bottle-green painted steel and brass catching it, the purple of the notes rich in the light. Same vault as the reference image. Light: one caged amber work lamp, deep bottle-green painted steel and brass catching it, the purple of the notes rich in the light. Outside the vault in a bottle-green corridor: the massive round steel vault door almost shut, a thin blade of amber light in the gap, a black-gloved hand already gripping the spoked brass locking wheel. No faces. Light: the amber light from the gap and one cold fluorescent tube above. Unretouched 35mm film still, rich saturated colour, fine grain. 16:9. Thanks.
